_comment: SHARED dual-transport fixture for the projects seam extension
(county-shading-and-project-stats, schema.md B.1/B.2, FR-24, FR-25, QA-25,
QA-26). Loaded by BOTH frontend/src/lib/checklistProjects.parity.test.ts and
backend/tests/test_checklist_projects_parity.py, so if either twin's
normalization drifts its own test fails.
Three blocks:
projIdRows      raw eBird `projId` -> the normalized string both
transports must produce ('' when absent or rejected).
projectIdsRows  raw eBird `projectIds` -> the normalized number array
([] when absent or rejected; bad ELEMENTS are dropped,
never coerced).
fieldFlagRows   the `fields=` query value -> the two skip flags each
transport derives from it.
THE TWO LIVE PARITY TRAPS, both of which are rows here rather than comments.
1. ANCHORS. Python's `$` matches BEFORE a trailing newline and
JavaScript's does not, so `re.match(r'^[A-Z0-9_]{1,32}$', 'EBIRD\n')`
succeeds where `.test()` fails. The Python half uses `re.fullmatch` for
exactly that reason, and the trailing-, leading- and embedded-newline
rows below are what hold it.
2. isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so a `projectIds: [true]` would
normalize to 1 there while `typeof true === 'boolean'` rejects it for
free in JS. The Python element guard must exclude bool explicitly. And
never int(v) / str.isdigit() on a STRING element: '١٠٥٠' parses as 1050
under both, which is why a string element is rejected outright rather
than coerced.
CHARACTER CLASSES. The v0.5.54 finding was a rust-regex `\d` admitting
Arabic-Indic digits while its JS twin did not, so both sides write EXPLICIT
ASCII classes ([A-Z0-9_]) and the fixture carries a non-ASCII-digit row.
A rejected value is '' / dropped, never invented: an unknown project is
shown as its raw identifier and a malformed one simply is not a project.

projIdRows.why: the generic eBird web/app portal, the commonest sampled value
the California atlas portal, the value this feature exists to report
Merlin: a submission portal, not a project (the display layer drops it, the seam keeps it)
ABSENT field (the key is omitted, so JS sees undefined and Python sees a missing key)
explicit null
a number, not a string: rejected outright, never String()-coerced
a boolean: rejected outright
an array: rejected outright
lowercase is outside the explicit ASCII class
mixed case is outside the class
AT CEILING: exactly 32 characters, the longest value the guard accepts
OVER CEILING: 33 characters, rejected so the persisted field is length-bounded
TRAILING NEWLINE: Python's `$` admits this and JavaScript's does not (the anchor trap). fullmatch is what makes them agree
LEADING newline
EMBEDDED newline
leading space
a hyphen is outside the class (eBird uses underscores)
NON-ASCII DIGITS (Arabic-Indic 012): a `\d`/`\w` class would admit these on the Python side only (v0.5.54)
empty string is below the {1,32} floor
digits and underscores alone are inside the class

projectIdsRows.why: the sampled shape: the California Breeding Bird Atlas
empty array
ABSENT field (the key is omitted, so JS sees undefined and Python sees a missing key)
explicit null
not an array
a STRING element is rejected, never coerced: int('١٠٥٠') is 1050 under both runtimes
NON-ASCII DIGIT STRING: the coercion trap in its live form
BOOLEAN element: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so this would become 1 without an explicit bool exclusion
a boolean beside a real id: only the boolean is dropped
non-integer float
negative
zero is a valid non-negative integer
AT CEILING: 999999999, the largest id the bound admits (9 digits, so the persisted number is length-bounded)
OVER CEILING: 1000000000
1e9 is the same over-ceiling value written as a float literal
AT the array cap: exactly MAX_PROJECT_IDS (8) elements are all kept
OVER the array cap: 9 elements truncate to the first 8
duplicates are kept RAW here and deduped at display (one checklist contributes one to a project)
a nested array element
a null element beside a real id

fieldFlagRows.why: absent: today's behavior, byte for byte
the shipped escapee pass: skips the location-name call only
the projects sweep: skips the location-name call AND the species resolution
the match is whole-string and CASE SENSITIVE, so this is unrecognized
`fields` stays single-valued whole-string equality: no comma splitting on either transport
an unrecognized value behaves exactly as an absent one
a trailing newline is not the flag (the anchor trap, in the flag table's own form)
